```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

XCNV annotates copy-number variants (CNVs) and scores them in two separate
lanes:

- **X-CNV**: the published X-CNV model (Zhang et al. 2021) gives each CNV an
  `MVP_score`, a model probability of pathogenicity. It is not a clinical class.
- **ACMG/ClinGen**: the 2019 constitutional CNV standard. Each criterion is one
  evidence row that you can inspect, change and rescore.

DuckDB does the overlap joins. R does validation, feature reduction, the tree
evaluator and scoring. No bedtools and no XGBoost are needed at run time.
Ownership, output contracts and validation rules are in
[`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Installation

```r
install.packages(
  "XCNV",
  repos = c("https://rgenomicsetl.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

## Example: a ClinVar deletion

The package includes the annotations for one real case, ClinVar allele 72461:
a pathogenic deletion that contains `SOX2`.

```{r real-case}
library(XCNV)
example <- xcnv_real_example()
example$clinvar[, c("clinvar_allele_id", "clinical_significance",
                    "grch37_chrom", "grch37_start0", "grch37_end0")]
```

### X-CNV score

```{r real-prediction}
prediction <- predict_cnv(example$cnv, example$resources)
prediction[, c("Chr", "Start", "End", "Type", "gain.freq", "loss.freq",
               "pLI", "Episcore", "GHIS", "MVP_score")]
```

### ACMG/ClinGen evidence and class

The deletion contains `SOX2`, an established haploinsufficient gene, so
criterion 2A gives one point.

```{r real-evidence}
cnv <- transform(example$cnv, cnv_id = example$clinvar$cnv_id,
                 cnv_type = type, assembly = "GRCh37")
genes <- transform(example$genes, assembly = "GRCh37")
dosage <- transform(example$dosage, assembly = "GRCh37")
evidence <- derive_cnv_2019_evidence(cnv, genes, dosage)
evidence[, c("criterion", "score", "source_id", "evidence_id")]
score_cnv_2019(evidence)[, c("cnv_id", "cnv_type", "score", "classification", "status")]
```

The automatic provider derives sections 1, 2A and 3 from gene and dosage
tables. Phenotype, inheritance, segregation, population, case and partial-gene
evidence are extra rows that you supply.

## GRCh38 calls

The X-CNV model and its resources are GRCh37. Declare a liftover to score
GRCh38 calls. XCNV lifts each call with DuckHTS and scores the GRCh37 interval:

```r
liftover <- xcnv_liftover(
  chain = "xcnv-resources/liftover/GRCh38_to_GRCh37.chain.gz",
  source_fasta = "GRCh38.fa", destination_fasta = "GRCh37.fa",
  source_assembly = "GRCh38", destination_assembly = "GRCh37",
  release = "ensembl-76-GRCh38_to_GRCh37"
)
predict_cnv(grch38_calls, resources, liftover = liftover)
```

The chain is Ensembl's GRCh38 to GRCh37 assembly mapping, which Ensembl
publishes without restriction on use. DuckHTS reads it compressed and matches
contigs with or without `chr`, so it lifts calls on a `chr1`-named GRCh38 FASTA
to a `1`-named GRCh37 FASTA as published.

The chain also maps GRCh38 regions to GRCh37 patch contigs (`HG1423_PATCH` and
others), which a primary GRCh37 FASTA such as `human_g1k_v37` lacks. DuckHTS
follows the chain and does not check the destination contig against the
destination FASTA. A call with an end in such a region is `unsupported`, with
`contig_changed` or `end_unmapped`. On 3,735 ClinVar copy-number records with
both GRCh38 and GRCh37 coordinates, lifted from the GIAB GRCh38 FASTA to
`human_g1k_v37`, the chain lifts 3,458 calls (92.6%); the same chain without
its patch-contig chains lifts 3,568 (95.5%) and changes no lifted interval.

Each row keeps its GRCh38 coordinates and adds the lifted interval. A call that
does not lift to one interval on the same contig and strand is `unsupported`,
with a `liftover_reason` and no `MVP_score`. The ACMG/ClinGen lane works on
GRCh38 directly.

## Resources

The resources are on Hugging Face at
[`RgenomicsETL/xcnv-resources`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/RgenomicsETL/xcnv-resources).
`SHA256SUMS` covers every file.

| Folder | Contents | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `grch37/` | X-CNV annotations and model | X-CNV lane |
| `grch38/` | GENCODE 50 genes and ClinGen dosage as Parquet, with `sources.tsv` | ACMG/ClinGen lane |
| `liftover/` | Ensembl GRCh38 to GRCh37 chain | X-CNV lane on GRCh38 calls |

Score calls with the X-CNV lane:

```r
resources <- xcnv_resources("xcnv-resources/grch37", require = "annotations")
predictions <- predict_cnv(read_cnv("input.bed"), resources)
write_xcnv(predictions, "predictions.output.csv")
```

`xcnv_resource_manifest()` lists the required files. `run_xcnv()` does the
same in one call.

Derive ACMG/ClinGen evidence for GRCh38 calls:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
genes <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "FROM 'xcnv-resources/grch38/genes.parquet'")
dosage <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "FROM 'xcnv-resources/grch38/dosage.parquet'")
calls <- data.frame(
  cnv_id = "sox2-del", chr = "chr3", start = 181700000, end = 181800000,
  cnv_type = "loss", assembly = "GRCh38"
)
evidence <- derive_cnv_2019_evidence(calls, genes, dosage)
score_cnv_2019(evidence)
```

On these relations the call above scores 1 point (2A, `SOX2`): pathogenic.

`tools/build_grch38_resources.R` rebuilds `grch38/` from SHA-256-pinned
sources.

## The model

The published classifier is one tree with 41 nodes. XCNV stores it as a small
table and evaluates it in R. `tools/stage_xcnv_model.R` rebuilds this table from
the original XGBoost booster and checks both evaluators on 1,024 rows; only that
maintainer step needs XGBoost.

[doi:10.1186/s13073-021-00945-4](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-021-00945-4).
